type: Photographic intensity-to-height relief; not an anatomical body fit
image_attribution: 2002 Shroud photographs published through Sindonology.org; contrast-enhanced versions by Rudolf Berwanger, Wikimedia Commons, 2022.
license: CC BY-SA 4.0, as declared on the source file pages
source_processing: The source file pages explicitly describe increased contrast. Pixel dimensions do not establish native optical resolution or a calibrated radiometric response. No AI upscaling or generative reconstruction was applied in this project.
mapping: Let v be 8-bit grayscale luminance. Set d=(255-v)/255, or its explicitly selected inverse. Coordinates x and y retain the crop aspect ratio. z=gain*100*(d-mean(d)); gain defaults to 0.65. Units are arbitrary. Mean subtraction translates the relief without altering its relative heights. No local normalization, anatomical adjustment, cloth-drape correction, inpainting, stain masking or manual feature sculpting is applied.
smoothing_encoding: Raw luminance is uint8; filtered luminance remains float32 to avoid introducing quantization terraces. The saved filtered PNG is 16-bit.
sampling: Read images with JPEG draft decoding at half dimensions, crop in documented original-image coordinates, then resample with Lanczos to the mesh grid. An optional separable Gaussian filter with sigma 4 mesh-grid pixels (truncated at 3 sigma) suppresses weave and JPEG noise. Both unblurred and blurred luminance maps are supplied.
limitations: Photographic exposure, enhanced contrast, stains, damage, weave, creases and illumination affect the height map. Depth has no physical calibration. This is an open surface, not a watertight human model. It cannot independently establish anatomy, identity, original image formation, or cloth-to-body distances.
